**Investigation paused at the fix-approach gate (Step 4).**

**What was measured.** No confirmation measurement is owed for this identity: it is a
Playwright in-run retry, which is already the empirical proof of non-determinism
(`1 flaky`, `106 passed`, `0 failed` in
https://github.com/growilabs/growi/actions/runs/34826447171 , job
`test-prod-node24 / run-playwright (chromium, 1/2, 8.0)`). The `flaky-repro` workflow's
project allowlist is vitest-only, so no repro request applies here.

**Root cause (Step 3 category: missing await / race in the test).** In
`apps/app/playwright/20-basic-features/inline-comment.spec.ts`, the body-popover
describe block creates the saved inline comment in its first test and there waits for the
highlight to actually exist before going on:

```ts
await expect
  .poll(async () =>
    page.evaluate(() => CSS.highlights.get('growi-inline-comment')?.size ?? 0),
  )
  .toBeGreaterThan(0);
```

The four later tests in the same block (lines ~2011, ~2040, ~2063, ~2077) each navigate to
the page again and then wait only for `inline-comment-ready` to be *attached* before
calling `clickText(page, targetSentence)` / `hoverText(...)`. That marker says the
SelectionCapture component reached its idle stage; it does not say the saved anchor has
been resolved and the hit-testable `CSS.highlights` Range registered. On a fresh load the
resolution is asynchronous, so a click can land before the Range exists, the hit test
matches nothing, no popover opens, and the very next line
(`await expect(popover).toBeVisible()`, line 2085) times out after 7000ms with
`element(s) not found` — exactly the recorded failure. The three sibling tests doing the
same sequence normally win the race, which is why this shows up as flakiness rather than
a hard failure.

**Fix approach reached (HIGH).** Test-side and surgical, one file: wait for
`CSS.highlights.get('growi-inline-comment')?.size > 0` after `inline-comment-ready` in the
four tests that interact with the highlight — the same poll the first test already uses —
ideally factored into a small helper next to `clickText` / `hoverText` so the next test
added to this block inherits it. No product-code change is implied.

**Why this is paused rather than fixed.** This run is the validation cycle for task 6.3 of
the `flaky-ci-closed-loop` spec, and the operator explicitly deferred Step 5 onward for
this run: no fix branch was pushed and no PR was opened. The investigation is therefore
complete up to and including the fix-approach decision, and stops there. Nothing is being
watched; the next routine run picks this issue up once a human has answered.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
- Recommendation: proceed with the fix above (wait for the `growi-inline-comment` highlight to be registered before clicking or hovering it, in the four body-popover tests).
